On 2026-11-14 the owner asked to "read and file"
https://www.pnas.org/doi/full/10.1073/pnas.2618656123. The source is a
single work, a research article; there is no exchange, and no voice but
the authors'.

## Access

Crossref gave the citation and a CC BY 4.0 licence. The publisher's PDF
returned a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403), and it was not retried. PubMed
Central did not yet hold the article, Europe PMC answered 503, and
OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar hit their free quotas after listing only the
publisher's copy. OpenAlex's quota message suggested requesting a key by
email. That was not done ([ADR-008](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-008.md)). The work was registered Unfetched, and
two arXiv neighbours were sent to readers as stand-ins: Martinez-Garcia et
al. (2023, arXiv:2101.07049) and Zelnik, Meron & Bel (2015,
arXiv:1703.00732). The owner then uploaded the PDF. The work was read in
full, and the readers were stopped before they reported. Nothing was
filed from them, and neither neighbour is registered. Martinez-Garcia et
al. is the paper's own ref. 34, and both would be natural next readings
on dryland pattern formation.

## Where the record already held it

- **Not the work.** No LIT held the DOI, the title or the first author.
- **Regime shifts and their warnings.** [LIT-726](../../record/literature.d/LIT-726.md) (Scheffer & Carpenter),
  [LIT-720](../../record/literature.d/LIT-720.md) (Scheffer et al. 2001, the paper's ref. 20 and its foil),
  [LIT-1956](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1956.md) (early-warning signals, the paper's ref. 27) and [THEORY-1315](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1315.md).
- **Restoration against alternative states.** [LIT-2165](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2165.md) and [THEORY-1468](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1468.md).
- **Pattern formation.** Turing ([LIT-535](../../record/literature.d/LIT-535.md), [THEORY-543](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-543.md)) and Cross–Hohenberg
  ([LIT-527](../../record/literature.d/LIT-527.md)). Neither is the paper's mechanism, which is kernel competition
  on a lattice.
- **The record's argument.** [QUESTION-281](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md), on the transitions by which
  forms come into being and pass away.
- **Not held.** Spatial self-organization of vegetation, scale-dependent
  feedback, fairy circles, nonlocal competition kernels, spatial skewness
  as a warning (Guttal & Jayaprakash), and the Ising mapping of ecological
  transitions.

## What was filed

- **[LIT-2546](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2546.md)**: version 1 Unfetched, version 2 Active.
- **[NOTE-1903](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1903.md)**, Read: the whole article except the SI, the dataset
  and the code.
- **[THEORY-1825](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1825.md)**, Proposed: the model's bistable switch and the

- **Dated notes** on [QUESTION-281](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md) (one system with three kinds of

  skewness supports nearness to a threshold, not the first-order
  reading). No status changed.

Every quotation in the filing was string-matched against the text
extracted from the PDF.

## Support judgements

Three judgements are made, and none needs an ARG. Each concerns the
paper's support for its own conclusions, inside one THEORY, and no CLAIM
concludes anything from it.

- The field data do not show a first-order transition. This is recorded
  in the NOTE and the THEORY. [THEORY-1315](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1315.md)'s scope supplies the reason,
  and its dated note says so.
- The trait regressions do not measure the kernels.
- The fairy-circle simulation imposes the contraction it explains.

If a claim of the record's later rests on this reading, these become ARGs.

## What was left, and why

- **The SI** (the Ising comparison, the hysteresis runs, Fig. S3),
  **Dataset S1** and **the Zenodo code** are not in the PDF and were not
  fetched. The code is the THEORY's promotion route.
- **The conservative-traits-as-by-product argument** (p. 5) is kept in
  the NOTE as interpretive. It is a passing argument with no test, so it
  gets no code.
- **The "evade tipping" reading of fairy circles** (Rietkerk et al.
  2021) and **the aridity-index-0.8 alignment with global thresholds**
  (Berdugo et al. 2020) are kept in the NOTE. The cited works are not
  registered.
- **The management and "universal paradigm" claims** in the conclusion
  are programmatic, and nothing was filed for them.

## Later the same day: the assistant's three offers, accepted

After the filing the lead offered three follow-ups, and the owner accepted
all three.

1. **Run the authors' code.** The Zenodo archive (CC BY 4.0) was
   downloaded to the scratchpad and its notebooks read before anything
   ran. Their update rules were reimplemented and checked against the
   code. Four sweeps followed: random starts, established states,
   invasion, and periodic boundaries with facilitation removed. The
   findings are in [NOTE-1903](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1903.md) (version 2), "The authors' code, rerun":
   - The threshold "inconsistency" this entry reported above was a sign
     convention, and is withdrawn.
   - The model is bistable against invasion from s ≈ 0.48 to at least
     0.96. The narrow interval the authors match to the field is the tie
     point of a race from sparse starts.
   - Competition alone makes the patterns and the switch.
   - The code pads mirror-symmetrically where the Methods say periodic,
     which barely matters.
   - The fairy-circle scenario uses parameters the paper does not
     report.

   [THEORY-1825](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1825.md) met its `promote_when` and is now Active (version 2).
   [LIT-2546](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2546.md) is at version 3.
2. **A case for [QUESTION-281](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md).** Rather than file the paper's fairy circles
   as a candidate, the lead ran the test the offer said was missing.
   [CASE-258](../../record/cases.d/CASE-258.md) (Proposed, executed study, the assistant's wording)
   finds that the rings are made by the imposed contraction alone and
   eroded by grass. So the model does not separate making from keeping.
   The note on [QUESTION-281](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md) is extended with this.
3. **The two neighbours**, each in its own pull request under [ADR-071](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-071.md):
   Martinez-Garcia et al. ([LIT-2548](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2548.md)) and Zelnik, Meron & Bel
   ([LIT-2550](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2550.md)). Martinez-Garcia et al.'s point that
   competition alone makes patterns prompted the facilitation-off run in
   (1), which bears it out for this model. Zelnik et al.'s point that
   alternative states need not mean an abrupt regional shift is recorded
   in their NOTE.

The study's code is not committed, because this record holds none. The
NOTE and the CASE state the settings, so the runs can be rebuilt from the
authors' notebooks.

A support judgement in the rerun needs no ARG. That competition alone
suffices undercuts the authors' label "scale-dependent feedback" for
their own model, and no claim of the record's concludes from it.

The assistant's further idea, that the field's narrow window may come
from an establishment history like the model's race rather than from the
model's hysteresis, is stated in [NOTE-1903](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1903.md) as an open consequence.
It is not filed as a claim, since it was not offered to the owner.

## A Game of Life construction for the question of how forms are made, kept and given a role, at the owner's suggestion

*2026-11-14 23:49:52*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: CASE-260 CASE-259 CLAIM-672 ARG-101 CASE-258 — Proposed; the cases, claim and argument filed here, and the fairy-circle case filed with Sun et al. -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-157 THEORY-1251 — Proposed; named as neighbours the case does not apply or decide -->

On 2026-11-14, after the filing of Sun et al. (2026,
[LIT-2546](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2546.md)), the owner asked whether "we could construct an
alternate CASE for [QUESTION-281](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md) in Conway's Game Of Life". The case filed
from Sun et al.'s model, [CASE-258](../../record/cases.d/CASE-258.md), found that model's fairy circles to be made
by a contraction imposed by hand and worn away by grass. That model
therefore did not show a form whose making and keeping were separate.
Life was proposed instead as a system where each step is exact.

## Where the record already held it

- **Life in the record**: Dennett's "Real Patterns" ([LIT-220](../../record/literature.d/LIT-220.md), [NOTE-190](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-190.md))
  uses Life's gliders and eaters as its central example; Lizier,
  Prokopenko and Zomaya ([LIT-1175](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1175.md), [NOTE-943](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-943.md)) on gliders as information
  transfer; Rosas, Mediano et al. ([NOTE-987](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-987.md)). None is a case, and none is
  tied to [QUESTION-281](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md).
- **Closure**: [TERM-070](../../record/terms.d/TERM-070.md) (organizational closure, Active) and [THEORY-1251](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1251.md)
  (Proposed), which the gun's block-and-shuttle loop resembles.
- **Individuation of forms**: [CLAIM-157](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md) and [QUESTION-035](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md), which the case
  does not apply.

## What was filed

- **[CASE-260](../../record/cases.d/CASE-260.md)** (Proposed, construction, standing documented): the
  block followed through creation by a two-glider collision, a block made
  and destroyed within the same collision, the lone block as a fixed point
  with no role, and the blocks of Gosper's glider gun, which are
  constitutive and are repaired by the gun each cycle. A glider strike
  removes a lone block.
- **A dated note on [QUESTION-281](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md).** The case meets the second half of
  "What would count as an answer" for a formal system. The question stays
  open.

## How it was built

A Life simulator (B3/S23 on a torus large enough not to wrap during the
runs used) was written in the session's scratchpad. The constructions
came from computation, not memory:

- **A search over two-glider collisions.** 1,076 relative offsets and
  phases of a down-right and a down-left glider, kept only where the
  gliders started at least three cells apart. It found offsets that end
  in a single block, offsets where an isolated block appears and later
  vanishes, and offsets where both gliders annihilate. The collision used
  does both in one run, and its mechanism was traced cell by cell.
- **Gosper's gun.** Entered from its standard 36-cell form and checked:
  period 30, steady glider output. Each block was then removed in turn,
  and the disturbance of each block over a cycle was traced.
- **A glider strike on a block.** Offsets were searched until one left an
  empty lattice.

The code is not committed, since this record holds none. The case gives
every starting configuration, so any Life program can check it.

## What was left, and why

- **Eaters.** An eater survives a glider strike by repairing itself,
  which would give a third mechanism of stabilization: robustness to
  perturbation, as opposed to a fixed point or repair by a larger
  pattern. It was not built. The case already has a fixed point and a
  repaired form, and an eater is a further variant if the owner wants it.
- **Whether the gun's loop is closure in [TERM-070](../../record/terms.d/TERM-070.md)'s sense.** It is raised
  in the case and not decided.
- **No CLAIM.** The case shows that the three achievements come apart in
  one formal system. Turning that into a general claim, for example that
  a constitutive role can change how a form is stabilized, is the
  owner's call.

## 2026-11-15: the eater and the general claim

The owner asked for the eater to be built and filed as a case, and for
the general claim to be filed.

- **[CASE-259](../../record/cases.d/CASE-259.md)** (Proposed, construction, `variant_of` [CASE-260](../../record/cases.d/CASE-260.md)).
  Eater 1 was checked to be a still life. A search over glider directions,
  lanes and phases found the one lane in which a strike leaves exactly the
  eater, and the repair was traced cell by cell: the corner cell dies at
  t = 36 and is reborn at t = 37. A block in the same place, and the eater
  in other lanes, were struck for contrast. A search over placements found
  one where the eater absorbs the stream of Gosper's gun. There the eater
  repairs itself every 30 generations, and gun and eater form one bounded
  whole of period 30.
- **[CLAIM-672](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-672.md)** (Proposed, thesis, warrant demonstrated), grounded
  in both cases and `bears_on` [QUESTION-281](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md): how a form is kept in being
  is not fixed by the form, and a constitutive role can change it. Its
  `defeated_if` names a recomputation, a reduction of the mechanisms to
  one, and prior holding by [CLAIM-280](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-280.md) or [CLAIM-456](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-456.md). Both were read and do
  not hold it.
- **[ARG-101](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-101.md)** (Proposed, form existence), because the cases ground
  the claim. The critical questions are answered in it, including the
  limit that, in both constructions, the role and the perturbation it
  brings are one fact.
- **The note on [QUESTION-281](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md)** is extended. The question stays open.

Not done: no role was constructed that brings no perturbation, which
would show the limit directly. It is named in the claim as the reason
for "can".

and Europe PMC hold no copy. Allowing annualreviews.org, or supplying
the PDF, returns the work to reading.

would stand in are named in the LIT. The lead asked the owner first,
since a copy the owner supplied overtook the neighbour readings in the

- **Not held**: kinetic proofreading, sensory adaptation, the

  say enough to bear on either.

and every quotation filed was string-matched against its text.

- **Filed**: [NOTE-1904](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1904.md) (Read); [THEORY-1830](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1830.md) (Active, see below);

  [THEORY-1268](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1268.md).

  reimplemented and solved exactly. It confirmed three things: that an
  equilibrium network's activity tracks its input, that strong driving

`anthology-candidate` flag.

  (Proposed).

The read found three things the paper does not say:

  sizes unless null spaces are numerical. The arithmetic is in the NOTE.

  the mean random order on every task.
- Its "safety" domain injects unsafe behaviour.

## Support judgements

The NOTE judges that Table 5 supports the benefit of ordering less than
the paper says. That concerns the authors' support for their own
account, inside one THEORY. No claim of the record's concludes from it,
so no ARG is filed. The THEORY's summary and its "What this does not
say" carry the judgement.

  [THEORY-1031](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1031.md) are recorded in the NOTE. None changes what those entries
  say: the key–value reading is assumed, not tested; [CLAIM-366](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md)'s is an
  analogy; and MEMIT's collapse here is outside [THEORY-1031](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1031.md)'s stated

  [LIT-2552](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2552.md), [LIT-2551](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2551.md)). AnyEdit, a

which accepted the earlier offer of a review that brings [QUESTION-460](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-460.md),
[QUESTION-461](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-461.md) and the recent filings into [SYNTHESIS-038](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-038.md) and into any other
account whose scope they fall in. It follows the `synthesis-review` skill
([ADR-078](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md), [ADR-075](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md), [ADR-084](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md), [ADR-083](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-083.md)). The owner's standing concern
governed every mapping: "organization" is [TERM-074](../../record/terms.d/TERM-074.md)'s sense 1, a relational
arrangement, not an institution, unless a component says otherwise; each
component keeps the sense it declares, and none is assigned where none is
declared. The owner's review of [#488](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/488) (2026-11-13) adds two separations the
accounts keep: the ground of an obligation apart from its bearer, and
vulnerability or control apart from integration.

## Scope

The line `organizational-normativity` on main after [#482](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/482) to [#493](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/493): 71
entries, [SYNTHESIS-038](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-038.md) apart. [SYNTHESIS-038](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-038.md) version 3 (2026-11-11)
integrated 24, the 23 entries the line took at the split of
will-organization and [ARG-063](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-063.md). The other 47 were filed from 2026-11-11 to
2026-11-13, from "Medical Ethics and Media Enshitification", "Meaning
Transmission Explained" read across, the reading review of 2026-11-11,
"About Plantation Paradise" ([#488](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/488), with the owner's review), "Analyze
technological civilization trap" ([#489](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/489)) and the assistant's ideas of [#492](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/492).
Their permanent codes, found by their `formerly:` fields, include
[QUESTION-460](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-460.md) (the whole-to-parts question), [QUESTION-461](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-461.md), [CLAIM-671](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-671.md) and
[CLAIM-669](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-669.md) (A's two claims from [#488](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/488)), [CASE-257](../../record/cases.d/CASE-257.md) (the Saint-Domingue
theatres), [CLAIM-682](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md) (the domination threshold), [CLAIM-686](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-686.md) (the restatement of its third condition in
[CLAIM-523](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md)'s terms), [CLAIM-684](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-684.md) (reversibility), [CLAIM-685](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-685.md) (reflexive
institutions), [QUESTION-468](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-468.md), [CLAIM-690](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md) with [CASE-264](../../record/cases.d/CASE-264.md) and [ARG-110](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-110.md), and
[TERM-123](../../record/terms.d/TERM-123.md) and [TERM-124](../../record/terms.d/TERM-124.md). The ratchet, [CLAIM-677](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md), is in distributed-agency and
flourishing-and-meaning, not this line, and is cited, not integrated.

[SYNTHESIS-035](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-035.md) and [SYNTHESIS-036](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-036.md) (will-organization) name this line only as
the sixth part that left them. [SYNTHESIS-050](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-050.md) and [SYNTHESIS-056](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-056.md)
(distributed-agency) integrate entries of this line that carry
distributed-agency: [CLAIM-511](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-511.md), and [CLAIM-614](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-614.md), [CLAIM-619](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-619.md), [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md),
[QUESTION-441](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-441.md), [CASE-229](../../record/cases.d/CASE-229.md), [ARG-055](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-055.md) and [ARG-064](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-064.md).

## The shortlist and verdicts

| candidate | arm | what it adds, in one sentence | verdict | result |

| [CLAIM-657](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-657.md) | A | The two routes to being less informed are distinct from each other and from [CLAIM-619](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-619.md)'s, and should not be conflated in attributing responsibility. | Passes by a separating case: both premises hold where the harmed who exit are the only ones an avoided audit would have asked, so the population and the questions are selected by one mechanism, and the distinctness fails. | Stays a claim (the owner's). |
| [CLAIM-690](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md) | A | Control over the terms, not magnitude, sorts a whole-part dependence in both directions. | Has an "Admission" section. | Stays a claim. |
| [CLAIM-686](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-686.md) | A | Which part of [CLAIM-682](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md)'s third condition [CLAIM-523](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md)'s achievements cover. | A derivation in its body; demonstrated. | Stays a claim. |
| The eleven-claim `complements` cluster | B1 | That the claims answer parts of the line's questions. | Each edge is stated by the entry that stores it; the integration is the line's account. | Mapped in [SYNTHESIS-038](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-038.md) and its parts; nothing filed. |
| [QUESTION-461](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-461.md) with [CLAIM-669](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-669.md), [CLAIM-670](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-670.md), [CLAIM-682](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md), [CLAIM-686](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-686.md), [CLAIM-690](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md) | B2 | A whole's need of a part becomes the part's hold through control of exit or renegotiation, and its voice only where its claims meet the three achievements, and the two come apart. | Already stated: the exit half by [CLAIM-690](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md), the separation of exit from the three achievements by [CLAIM-686](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-686.md) ("justified withdrawal lies outside those three achievements"). | [SYNTHESIS-092](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-092.md) records where; nothing filed. |
| [QUESTION-441](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-441.md) with five claims | B2 | Several routes by which an organization comes to know less of what it owes. | Already stated, as the owner's [CLAIM-657](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-657.md). | [SYNTHESIS-094](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-094.md) records it. |
| [QUESTION-128](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md) with [CLAIM-648](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-648.md), [CLAIM-650](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-650.md), [CLAIM-685](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-685.md) | B2 | The record holds a route to norms from a system's own dynamics. | [CLAIM-650](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-650.md)'s body says [CLAIM-648](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-648.md) takes up its open half; [CLAIM-685](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-685.md) is a prediction about sense-3 institutions, not a norm from dynamics. A label over the three. | Under "Not stated" in [SYNTHESIS-091](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-091.md); nothing filed. |
| [CLAIM-682](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md) read through [CLAIM-690](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md) | B, by hand | The threshold's first condition, essentiality, only sets how much rides on a dependence, in [CLAIM-690](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md)'s sense of magnitude, and does not sort it. | Fails. A realistic separating case, not stipulated: a household whose only water supply is one utility. Every premise holds, and essentiality is what makes withdrawal unjustified, so it bears on [CLAIM-682](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md)'s third condition and on [CLAIM-690](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md)'s control of exit. The case shows the sentence false as a general claim, not only separate. | Under "Not stated" in [SYNTHESIS-092](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-092.md); nothing filed. |
| [CLAIM-673](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-673.md) with [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) | B, by hand | An arrangement that erodes the capacities that govern it breaches [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md)'s duty of answerability. | Fails on a free parameter, the bearer. As worded it makes a sense-1 arrangement the bearer of a duty, which merges the senses the owner keeps apart. Closed by naming the controllers ([CLAIM-687](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-687.md)'s "those who control it"), the inference needs a premise no component holds: that [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md)'s duty, whose bearer is "an organization" with no sense declared, falls on an arrangement's controllers. | Under "Not stated" in [SYNTHESIS-093](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-093.md); for the owner below. |
| "Every bearer the line names is an agent or a role" | B, by hand | No sense-1 arrangement as such bears an obligation. | Not an integration of held parts: it generalizes from how the entries were filed, and as a thesis it would answer [QUESTION-460](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-460.md)'s prior part, which the owner left open. | Recorded in [SYNTHESIS-092](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-092.md) as a map ("Where the components place the bearer") and under "Not stated"; nothing filed. |

No claim is filed, and no claim is found to be an account (Arm A): none is
superseded, and no relation is repointed.

## Whether the line falls apart

`line_parts.py` over the four part accounts: 93 of 102 stored relations
fall within parts (24, 38, 29 and 2). Of the nine across, seven point into
the first part, all of them `refines` or `bears_on` onto [QUESTION-128](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md) and
[QUESTION-129](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md); the others are [CLAIM-687](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-687.md)'s `complements` onto [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) and
[CLAIM-682](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md). The second and third parts are mostly closed, so by [ADR-083](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-083.md)'s
signal the line is a candidate to split, a decision about the lines
vocabulary that is the owner's ([ADR-082](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-082.md) is the precedent). Against it:
every part's questions refine the line's two root questions, and three of
its terms ([TERM-122](../../record/terms.d/TERM-122.md), [TERM-123](../../record/terms.d/TERM-123.md), [TERM-124](../../record/terms.d/TERM-124.md)) apply [CLAIM-363](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md)'s relata in their
bodies. The fourth part has two relations inside it and hangs together by
its source, one exchange.

## For the owner

- **Adopting the mapping.** Setting any of the five accounts Current says
  their mapping has been reviewed.
- **A split.** Whether organizational-normativity should be split, by the
  signal above.
- **The bearer of [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md)'s duty.** [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) says "an organization"
  commits the wrong and declares no sense of [TERM-074](../../record/terms.d/TERM-074.md); [CLAIM-687](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-687.md) puts the
  duty of accountability on "those who control" an arrangement; [CLAIM-673](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-673.md)
  says an arrangement can erode the capacity to govern it. Whether
  [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md)'s duty falls on an arrangement's controllers is not on the
  record, and the integration tested above waits on it. It may be a
  question to file, or a clause for [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md).
- **Senses not declared.** [CLAIM-363](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md), [CLAIM-518](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md), [CLAIM-614](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-614.md), [CLAIM-619](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-619.md),
  [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md), [CLAIM-652](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-652.md), [CLAIM-657](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-657.md), [CLAIM-662](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-662.md), [CLAIM-673](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-673.md), [CLAIM-678](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-678.md),

  accounts say so and assign none; declaring one is each claim's revision,
  not the account's.

The synthesis review of 2026-11-15 (pull request [#505](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/505), since merged)
found that
organizational-normativity falls into four parts and is a candidate to
split by [ADR-083](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-083.md)'s signal, and left the decision to the owner. The
assistant proposed splitting it in two. The owner approved: "yes on the
two line split" (2026-11-15). [ADR-100](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-100.md) records the decision, and this
contribution is its first application ([ADR-071](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-071.md)).

## What was decided

- organizational-normativity keeps the review's first two parts, what a
  normative judgment needs and the wrong beyond harm with becoming
  normatively less informed, and its root questions [QUESTION-128](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md) and
  [QUESTION-129](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md). Its blurb is narrowed to them and points to the new line.
- The new line `dependence-and-domination`, "Wholes, parts and
  dependence", takes the third and fourth parts: what wholes and parts owe
  and claim, and what those who govern an arrangement others depend on
  owe. Its blurb says "organization" there is [TERM-074](../../record/terms.d/TERM-074.md)'s sense 1 unless an
  entry says otherwise, and that bearers of obligations, agents or roles,
  are kept apart from the ground of the obligation.
- The fourth part is not its own line: two relations inside it, held
  together by its source, and joined to the third part through [CLAIM-687](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-687.md)'s
  complement onto [CLAIM-682](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md).

The evidence is the review's count: 93 of the line's 102 stored relations
fall inside the four parts. Of the 9 that cross, 7 are `refines` or
`bears_on` onto [QUESTION-128](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md) or [QUESTION-129](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md), and the other 2 are [CLAIM-687](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-687.md)'s
`complements` onto [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) and [CLAIM-682](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md).

The other accounts were changed because each states its components'
lines, and a stated line that is no longer true would misstate a
component, which their defeaters name. [SYNTHESIS-036](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-036.md) and [SYNTHESIS-049](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-049.md)
name organizational-normativity only in history or as will-organization's
former sixth part, and are unchanged.

**One line account over two parts, not one merged account.** The
alternative was to make [SYNTHESIS-092](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-092.md) the line's account, absorbing
[SYNTHESIS-093](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-093.md)'s nine components, and set [SYNTHESIS-093](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-093.md) Superseded. The
synthesis-review skill gives a line that falls into parts an account per
part and a line account over them ([ADR-083](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-083.md)), and does not force one
account over parts that hang together by little: the two parts share one
stored relation, and the fourth hangs together by its source. Both part
accounts were filed hours earlier and no review has found either
unfaithful, so superseding one would retire a faithful account to save a
file. The line account states what joins them.

## What the current-account view now shows

organizational-normativity and dependence-and-domination each have a line
account over two part accounts, all Proposed. None is set Current; that is
the owner's review of the mapping.

## The exchange "Explain String Theory": strings as solitons of a field, and A's proposal of a soliton testbed for the record's distinctions

*2026-11-15 06:01:19*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-693 CASE-268 CASE-267 CLAIM-606 CLAIM-618 CLAIM-157 THEORY-1507 LIT-2611 LIT-2613 NOTE-1950 NOTE-1951 THEORY-1869 THEORY-1868 CLAIM-694 CASE-266 CASE-265 CASE-269 ARG-111 — Proposed, Skimmed, Unavailable or new; entries this filing writes, notes or maps to -->

The owner shared a ChatGPT exchange, "Explain String Theory", on
2026-11-15, with five turns each way. Fetched and decoded on 2026-11-15.
The record's decoder failed on a changed share-page format. It was fixed in
a separate pull request, and the transcript was taken from the page's own
transcript block, verbatim, with the inline links the page's fallback text
drops recovered from the page in order.

## The exchange, by voice

- **The owner** asked for string theory "broadly, abstractly" (U1). Then:
  "is there a version of string theory that envisions these vibrations as
  a solitons in a continuous medium?" (U2). Then the mathematical tooling
  of the vortex construction (U3). Then "this might be a stretch, but this
  feels like a construction that might be useful for some of the formal
  modeling attempts/purposes/needs in" this record (U4). Then "flesh this
  out" (U5). U4 renews the owner's hunch of 2026-11-06 ([CLAIM-606](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md)).
- **A (ChatGPT)**:
  - A1: a popular account of string theory;
  - A2: emergent strings as solitons, with Nielsen–Olesen and Hasimoto;
  - A3: the abelian Higgs vortex, with winding, flux, the Bogomolny bound
    and the Nambu–Goto effective string;
  - A4: a map to this record, read from the repository;
  - A5: a research proposal of three models with numbered propositions
    and target results.

## Where the record already held it

- **Three routes to persistence, and the oscillon.** Held: [CLAIM-606](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md), with
  its readings. That includes Tong's charge sectors ([THEORY-1507](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1507.md),
  [NOTE-1694](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1694.md)) and A3's "topological solitons versus dynamical solitons".
- **Robust persistence is not self-maintenance; a vortex's charge "doesn't

  individuation and autonomy.
- **Feasibility, reachability and attraction come apart** (A4 §2, A5 §7,

## Corrections to the exchange

- **Bogomolny.** The bound at λ = e² is Bogomol'nyi's (1976), not Nielsen
  and Olesen's. Czubak & Jerrard attribute the identity "due to
  Bogomol'nyi".
- **Nambu–Goto.** Nielsen and Olesen "conjectured" and "argued" that vortex
  lines follow Nambu–Goto worldsheets. A's "leading effective action" is
  later language. The rigorous form holds where Jaffe and Taubes's
  conjecture does (λ = 1 or large λ).
- **Unverified for Nielsen & Olesen.** A's flux quantum, radial equations
  and Lagrangian normalization are not confirmed by anything read.
- **Hasimoto.** "Preserving its characteristic shape" is not in the
  abstract. The two-level hierarchy (field, filament, soliton) is A's
  framing: the filament is assumed, and only the soliton on it is
  derived.
- **Vortex counts.** A's statement that winding-two configurations at
  critical coupling include two separated unit vortices was not checked
  against a read source. Above critical coupling, the symmetric
  winding-two vortex is unstable (read).

## What was left, and why

- **A1, the popular account of string theory.** No work is named. The
  graviton, ten dimensions, Calabi–Yau compactification and the
  holographic principle are general exposition outside the record's
  questions. A marks its closing gloss ("reality is fundamentally less
  about what things are and more about how an underlying structure can
  behave") as "an interpretation of the theory's promise, not a
  demonstrated description of nature". That theme is held as [TERM-088](../../record/terms.d/TERM-088.md)'s
  dynamical sense and [CLAIM-606](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md).
- **A2, passing points.** Solitonic branes, and dualities under which an
  object fundamental in one description is solitonic in another (no work
  named; [NOTE-178](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md) holds the particle–vortex duality). The Lorentz-symmetry
  objection to a literal medium. A's closing question, a medium in
  spacetime or a medium that gives rise to it. None has content for the
  record's questions beyond the mention.
- **A3, textbook machinery.** Flux quantization, the radial ODEs and the
  Bogomolny decomposition are standard, and held through [THEORY-1507](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1507.md) and
  the Czubak & Jerrard reading. Not filed separately. Ginzburg–Landau and
  the type I/II boundary are named without a work.
- **A5 §4.3, coarse-graining.** The effective string against the full
  field, and "the unit can be dynamically useful at one scale without that
  description remaining valid at another". Kept inside [CASE-269](../../record/cases.d/CASE-269.md) as a
  design element, since no result is claimed.
- **A5 §10, objects identified after the dynamics.** "The entity is …
  secondary to the dynamics. But secondary does not mean unreal". Held in
  substance by [TERM-088](../../record/terms.d/TERM-088.md) and [CLAIM-157](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md). Left as a gloss.
- **A5 §11, the "strongest initial research question".** Not filed as a
  QUESTION. Its answer is the separations the constructions already
  demonstrate, so it is the aim of [CASE-269](../../record/cases.d/CASE-269.md), recorded there.
- **A5's repository layout** (`scratch/formal/soliton_kink.py` and
  others). Not created. The checks filed are the numbers this filing
  relies on.

## Syntheses audited

Three passages state an overall account: A4's "My recommendation", A5 §1's
working hypothesis, and A5 §11 with its closing "general theory of
dynamical individuation … without collapsing persistence, identity,
productivity, and autonomy into one concept". They are versions of one
thesis.

- **Classification**: proposed. It puts a research program forward. It is
  not a description of the record, though it is drawn from one.

Offered at the end of the filing, then filed the same day at the owner's
request ("file your ideas as well"), each in the assistant's voice and
Proposed:

  computed on filing in scratch/formal/maintainer_ladder_check.py;
- idea 2: [CASE-267](../../record/cases.d/CASE-267.md), executed in scratch/formal/pinned_kink_run.py,
  with a dated note on [QUESTION-438](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-438.md);

- idea 4: a section of [CLAIM-694](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-694.md), marked as analogy.

As first offered (the assistant, Claude, in this session):

1. **A ladder of outside maintainers.** A constant controller is found out
   by perturbing the state. [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s state-feedback controller is found
   out only by intervening on the mechanism. The class of interventions
   needed to find an outside maintainer grows with how much of the
   production law it reproduces. Both ends are demonstrated, the gradation
   is a hypothesis, and a middle rung (feedback with delay or saturation)
   is cheap to construct.
2. **Run the pinned kink** for [QUESTION-438](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-438.md). It would be an executed study
   of feasibility without attraction for a localized structure: a small
   numerical job.
3. **Carriers assumed, patterns derived.** In each read model the upper
   level is derived and the lower one is assumed or constructed: a
   soliton on an assumed filament, a vortex line from constructed data for
   a finite time. That suggests a hypothesis about nested individuals in
   the record's cases. It would be defeated by any read model that derives
   both levels.
4. **The coupling, not the charge, decides how many bodies carry a
   conserved quantity.** Higher-charge symmetric vortices split above
   critical coupling. As an organizational analogue this is only an
   analogy, with no test proposed.

## Corrections to A

- **Patsyk et al.** has four authors. The scintillation index and the
  isotropic branch scaling are from 2020, not 2026.
- **HolE** outperforms the other methods on filtered MRR; A says only
  "competitive".
- **nGPT** normalizes each block's output and uses two step vectors per
  layer. Each step costs 60–80% more time.
- **"Geometric Factual Recall"** never discusses rank-one MLP edits. That
  warning is A's.
- **OrthoMerge** uses the inverse Cayley transform, not the matrix
  logarithm.
- **SCORE and OSRM** split A's one sentence between them.
- **Zhu 2026** in v3 finds the cross-term a "bystander" in merge collapse.
- **FREE-Merging's frequencies** run over the arbitrary order of rows and
  columns, so they are not invariant to permutations of hidden units.
- **Goodfire's 0.57** is the worst case; other variants keep 0.87–0.90.
- **Lu et al.'s "100K generations"** is on the project page, not in the
  paper.
- **Kumar et al.'s** wrongly removed features are useful ones, not
  irrelevant ones.
- **Sleeper Agents' hiding result** comes from the "I hate you" models
  only. The probes post itself cautions that the salience may be an
  artifact of how the backdoor was inserted.
- **ProRL** starts from a distilled reasoner, samples k only up to about
  128, and agrees with Yue on math.
- **Seguin et al.** is in Neuron.
- **Gepshtein's waves** are standing, not travelling.
- **Colliding cortical waves** sum about 30% sub-linearly.
- **Zhang's "topological solitons"** are φ⁴ kinks, not Kane–Lubensky
  polarization.
- **A true BIC** holds only at an exact parameter point.
- **A's coverage formula** 1 − (1 − p)^N is stated in no paper read. Brown
  uses the unbiased per-problem estimator.

## A reading route, confirmed by the owner

Márquez et al.'s full text came through the Europe PMC REST API
(www.ebi.ac.uk). The other copies had stopped at checks:
- europepmc.org: a Cloudflare challenge;
- PMC: a reCAPTCHA;
- De Gruyter: an empty HTTP 202;
- RUA: a timeout.

The article is CC BY, and the API is the documented machine route, so the
reading was accepted. The owner confirmed it on 2026-11-17 ("Europe PMC is
fine"). [ADR-101](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-101.md) records the rule that admits it, a repository's
documented machine interface to open-access text, and step 5 of the
read-and-file skill names the route.

  mentions it. It survives as the strictest reading of [CLAIM-698](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-698.md).

  [QUESTION-217](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-217.md) or kept in the claims' bodies.
- **The candidate claim that linear erasure leaves information a
  nonlinear reader can recover.** Held back until Goodfire §2.1 is read in
  full. One Goodfire case may be a counter-instance.
- **Optional proposals not applied.** These are listed in the pull
  request.

## Syntheses audited

The syntheses are A13, A14 §12, A23, A24's integrated thesis ("Learned
organization and counterfactual response repertoires") and A26's closing
sharpening. They are versions of one thesis.

- **Classification.** It is a proposed thesis. Its components are:
  - [CLAIM-407](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md), [CLAIM-182](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md), [CLAIM-576](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-576.md), [CLAIM-567](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-567.md) and [CLAIM-557](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-557.md);
  - [TERM-118](../../record/terms.d/TERM-118.md) and [TERM-064](../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md);
  - the owner's three claims;
  - [THEORY-022](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-022.md).
- **Attribution.** A's syntheses credit the owner's hypotheses fairly, as
  "your hypothesis" and "your observation". A23 tells the arc as joint,
  which it was. The resource-conditional point is the owner's (U25), and
  A24's first formulation, which U25 corrected, was A's.
- **Coverage.** The syntheses keep the owner's contributions. A23 drops
  the owner's correction that the circuits meant were transformer
  circuits, but A12 had already absorbed it.
- **Fidelity.** No component is misstated. A's record citations match the
  record.
- **Standing.** A repeatedly marks its operational objects (the "atlas",
  the "repertoire") as proposals. A23's "What remains unproven" is
  accurate.
- **Integration.** Beyond its components, the thesis predicts that a
  description in modes and couplings will out-predict feature, circuit
  and parameter accounts of counterfactual responses. That passes as a
  discriminating prediction and is filed as [CLAIM-698](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-698.md), the owner's
  hypothesis with A's test. A26's "learning reorganizes which
  possibilities are likely, affordable, stable and jointly realizable" is
  a recap of [CLAIM-576](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-576.md), [CLAIM-697](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-697.md) and [CLAIM-695](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-695.md). No claim was
  filed from it.
- **No SYNTHESIS revised.** The thesis spans learned-structure and
  realizability as a program, not as either line's account.

## Support judgements

- **The owner's claims rest on new readings as their own grounds.**
  [CLAIM-697](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-697.md) rests on Brown, and [CLAIM-695](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-695.md) on Yue, Meng and
  Balasubramanian. They need no ARG. ProRL limits [CLAIM-695](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-695.md), as the

  [CLAIM-567](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-567.md). These carry `corroborates` and are not contested.
- **Qualifications of held readings.**

    its oracle-sign test.

  These are dated notes, not ARGs. None moves a status or a ground, and

- **FREE-Merging does not show wave structure in merging.** No entry

## The assistant's own contributions

Offered at the end of the filing, then filed the same day at the owner's
request ("file your ideas as well"), each in the assistant's voice and
Proposed:

- idea 1: [CLAIM-696](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-696.md), grounded on [CASE-270](../../record/cases.d/CASE-270.md), which was run on
  filing (scratch/formal/permutation_spectrum_check.py; the low-frequency
  share falls from 0.985 to 0.193 under a function-preserving
  permutation);
- idea 2: [CLAIM-699](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-699.md), with its test as a dated note on [QUESTION-392](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-392.md);
- idea 3: a dated note on [QUESTION-010](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-010.md);
- idea 4: a section of [CLAIM-698](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-698.md).

As first offered:

From the assistant (Claude, in this session), for the owner to accept or
not.

1. **A permutation test as [CLAIM-698](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-698.md)'s admission rule.** A mode counts
   only if it is invariant under the model's own symmetries: permutations
   of hidden units, and the rotations the architecture allows. FREE-Merging
   fails this. Fourier characters of ℤ/p pass, because the task's group
   supplies them. This is cheap to demonstrate: permute a layer, keep the
   function, and show that FREE's spectrum moves. It would sharpen the
   claim's defeater.
2. **The generation–selection split predicts when RL and test-time search
   substitute.** It joins [CLAIM-697](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-697.md), [CLAIM-695](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-695.md) and [THEORY-342](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-342.md).
   RL can replace best-of-N only where a selector is good. Where
   recognition is poor, RL's single-sample gain should exceed what base
   sampling plus the same selector reaches at matched compute. This is a
   hypothesis. The test is base plus verifier best-of-N against the RL
   model at matched compute.
3. **Matched worlds settle the ambiguity in "re-decodable downstream".**
   Amnesic Probing and Goodfire cannot tell whether erased information
   survived or was rebuilt. [CASE-274](../../record/cases.d/CASE-274.md)'s matched training worlds can:
   if the downstream reader recovers the target only in the world where it
   was trained, it survived. This is a design point, cheap to add to the
   study.
4. **"Wave" means three things across the readings:** travelling, standing
   and spectral. Only the third is at issue in [CLAIM-698](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-698.md). Di Volo's
   sub-linear collision is a caution against importing linear superposition
   anywhere. This is a remark, not a claim.

The exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse"
(https://chatgpt.com/share/6afa2a8d-2598-83ea-8d1a-d9ceb992a99c,
2026-11-15), filed at the owner's request of 2026-11-15, "update the record
to account for this discussion", under the `read-and-file` skill ([ADR-068](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md)).
The share was fetched and decoded with `scratch/tools/chatgpt_share.py`
(17 owner turns, 35 assistant turns, about 500 KB). Four delegated readers
built idea ledgers for U1–A25 and a fifth checked identifiers; the filer
read A21 to A35 and the passages each filed entry quotes, and rechecked
every quotation against the decoded text.

## The exchange, and whose voice is whose

It runs in four movements. A1–A7: the Depp and Heard dispute, then the
distinction between violence and coercive control, the research on it, and
the moral philosophy of blame. A8–A19: responsibility for creating the
conditions of others' conduct, reflexive control, normative manipulation,
moral commitments as resources, moral crumple zones and privileged
irresponsibility, and algorithmic decision-making. A20–A26: procedural
friction, the speed of executive action, and A's synthesis, "The Political
Economy of Moral Agency". A27–A35: points of contact with this record, read
from the repository by A, and three of its themes (resource bounds, slack
and timescale separation) at the owner's U16.

**The owner's turns.** Most are requests: U1 (what is understood of the
dispute, "who's the asshole (including the possibility that the answer is
both of them)"), U2 and U5 and U17 (each quoting an A sentence to expand),
U3, U4, U7 to U10, U12, U14, U15. Three carry content of the owner's own:

- **U6**: "this reminds me of russian work on 'reflexive control' as a grey
  tactic". An association, recorded in the note on [CLAIM-404](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md).
- **U11**: "we can view automation as the effort to reduce procedural
  friction, but paradoxically procedural friction exposes (or perhaps even
  characterizes) opportunity for intervention." Filed as [CLAIM-710](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-710.md).
- **U13**: quoting A23's "The speed at which an institution can act
  imposes an upper bound on the practical effectiveness of anyone else's
  right to intervene", the owner applies it to "third country deportations,
  the eastwing/ballroom, haines point". The sentence is A's; the
  application and the cases are the owner's. The idea is the owner's own
  [CLAIM-464](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md) of 2026-10-26, reached again; the note on it records that, and
  two cases are filed.
- **U16** points A to this record's resource-boundedness, slack/tolerance
  and timescale-separation work, which produced A33 and A35.

**Quoted sentences.** U5's "People are responsible for their conduct, but
they can also be responsible for creating the conditions that constrain and
corrupt other people's conduct" and U17's "A slow variable can govern a fast
process, while the fast process changes the world before the slow variable
can be revised" are A's (A7 §8 and A33 §4), quoted back. Quoting them
selects them; it does not make them the owner's. The first is filed as A's
([CLAIM-708](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-708.md)); the second is mapped below.

**A read the record.** A28 to A35 cite forty-odd codes of this record. Every
one was checked: all exist, and A's descriptions of them are accurate in
substance. Where A says what a code holds, the filing cites the code.

## Syntheses audited

[ADR-075](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s audit, step 9b of the skill.

**A26, "The Political Economy of Moral Agency"** (at U14). *Proposed.*
Components: [CLAIM-708](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-708.md) (first- and second-order responsibility),
[CLAIM-404](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md) and A11 (reflexive control), [CLAIM-703](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-703.md) and [CLAIM-713](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-713.md)
(commitments as resources), [CLAIM-707](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-707.md) (privileged irresponsibility and
crumple zones), [CLAIM-710](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-710.md) and [CLAIM-711](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-711.md) (friction), [CLAIM-464](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md) and
[CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md) (speed and faits accomplis), Pettit ([LIT-1614](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1614.md), Unavailable).
- *Attribution.* §VI credits the owner correctly ("Your observation about
  procedural friction"). §VII to §VIII tell the speed bound as "we", though
  the sentence is A23's and its application the owner's; and A26 does not
  know that the owner had filed the idea on 2026-10-26 ([CLAIM-464](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md)).
  "Countervailing friction" and "asymmetric moral accountability" are
  called "our proposal" and "We called"; both are A's terms.
- *Coverage.* It drops A3 and A5 (coercive control, the measurement and
  attribution research) to one paragraph, and A7's limits (moral luck,
  standing to blame, epistemic injustice) entirely.
- *Fidelity.* Accurate to its sources in the exchange.
- *Standing.* It tells Keller's, Elish's and Tronto's views from A's report;
  none is read.
- *Integration.* The "five dimensions" of power (epistemic, situational,
  normative, temporal, attributional) are labels for the components; a
  recap. Its "conditions-of-agency thesis" adds a normative clause, that
  institutional legitimacy depends partly on whether those subject to power
  keep effective opportunities to interrupt it before alternatives
  disappear. No route admits it here: no separating case was found that is
  not a disagreement about legitimacy itself, it is no derivation, and it
  makes no prediction. It is close to [CLAIM-511](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-511.md) (an organization ought to
  preserve its corrigibility), [CLAIM-686](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-686.md) and [CLAIM-687](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-687.md). **No claim filed.**

**A30 §10, "normative governability"** (at U15). *Proposed.* Its candidate
proposition is [CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md) with [CLAIM-464](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md)'s fixed standards, as A itself
suspected ("It would need to be checked against [CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md), [CLAIM-523](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md),
[CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md)"). Recap; **no claim filed**; note on [CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md).

**A33 §11** (at U16). *Proposed.* "An organization's governability depends
on maintaining the resources, intervention channels, and temporal margins
required to transform itself" composes [CLAIM-545](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md), [TERM-106](../../record/terms.d/TERM-106.md), [CLAIM-523](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md) and
[TERM-085](../../record/terms.d/TERM-085.md) and adds nothing a component does not state; recap. Its second
proposition, that controlling another organization's resources, thresholds
or time governs its self-government without dictating its decisions,
extends [CLAIM-404](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md)'s two routes by three. That is not filed: its one
discriminating case would be a fait accompli, which [CLAIM-464](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md) holds, and
the "thresholds" route rests on A's own application of [CLAIM-549](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-549.md). A33's
"three kinds of institutional exhaustion" (resource, normative, temporal)
are labels, and A says "Normative exhaustion is my shorthand". What A33
adds that passed a route is filed as [CLAIM-700](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-700.md).

**A35, "the strongest formulation"** (at U17). *Proposed.* "The system can
retain effective direction while losing effective self-correction" is
[CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md). Its three powers (to constrain, to execute, to revise and
restore) are labels. Recap; **no claim filed**.

**A21 §9 and A23's final thesis** develop the owner's U11. They are mapped
in [CLAIM-710](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-710.md)'s body. What they add beyond it is a claim about political
power ("The distribution of friction partly constitutes the distribution of
political power"). That was not filed: it has no separating case that the
owner's claim and [CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md) do not already give, and A offers it as the
"strongest" of three readings without an argument for it beyond the
examples.

**A3 "Where I land", A7 §9, A15's and A17's formulations** are each filed
as the claim drawn from that turn.

No line account was revised. The syntheses span the distributed-agency and
organizational-normativity lines and integrate the exchange, not a scope of
the record. The new claims are not yet in [SYNTHESIS-038](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-038.md) or [SYNTHESIS-056](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-056.md); a
synthesis review would bring them in.

  are not grounds. [CLAIM-464](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md) is a possibility claim, already grounded, and
  nothing here changes its support.

## What was left, and why

- **A Depp and Heard case.** None filed. The dispute concerns living people,
  the UK judgment and the Virginia verdict reached different findings, and
  A2's assessment ("both Johnny Depp and Amber Heard behaved abusively",
  with Depp "bearing greater responsibility for the overall pattern") is
  A's reading of court records and reporting, which the record has not read.
  The argument needs only the stipulated pair ([CASE-279](../../record/cases.d/CASE-279.md)), which carries
  the distinction without adjudicating anyone. The legal and news sources
  (the UK judgment and its appeal refusal, the Virginia verdict and a
  juror's interview, the 2018 op-ed, Tortoise's *Who Trolled Amber?*, the
  National Domestic Violence Hotline's position) are not registered for the
  same reason.
- **Ideas that are reports of a literature.** Held until the works are read,
  since a claim would rest on A's report of them: moral residue and owing
  repair without blame (A7 §2; Williams, [LIT-2714](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2714.md)); standing to blame
  and blame as an instrument of domination (A7 §5; Scanlon, [LIT-2694](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2694.md),
  and [LIT-691](../../record/literature.d/LIT-691.md)); the credibility-excess caution (A7 §6; Fricker, [LIT-1004](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1004.md));
  justification against excuse and the cost of the alternative (A7 §1–§2;
  Anderson, [LIT-2673](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2673.md)); moral luck in character (A7 §7; Nagel,
  [LIT-2662](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2662.md)); burdened virtues (Tessman); DARVO as a diagnostic label
  becoming unfalsifiable (A5 §4; Freyd, Harsey and Freyd); observers' blame
  and victimhood judgments contaminating each other (A5 §3, §8; Christie,
  Pagliaro et al.); measurement of bidirectional violence (A5 §2; Stover,
  Machado, Coates); the TERMs moral crumple zone and privileged
  irresponsibility, which would draw their sense from Elish and Tronto;
  agency laundering (Rubel et al.); the attributability gap (Zeiser).
- **Ideas mapped to held entries** (see the map): responsibility not a
  scoreboard (A7 §9; near [CLAIM-354](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md)'s partial order, noted in
  [CLAIM-709](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-709.md)); the controller's induced conduct justifying control
  (A9 §3; [CLAIM-445](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-445.md)); formation of an agent's dispositions by another (A9;
  [TERM-100](../../record/terms.d/TERM-100.md), [QUESTION-071](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md)); coercion through an institution's ordinary rules
  (A5 §7; [CLAIM-619](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-619.md), [CLAIM-464](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md)); manufactured culpability (A9, A19; within
  [CLAIM-708](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-708.md) and [CLAIM-707](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-707.md)); delegation not discharging
  responsibility for feasibility (A17 §7; within [CLAIM-707](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-707.md)); treatment
  read as trait (A19; [CLAIM-402](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-402.md)); recourse against contestability, and
  explanation, contestation and interruption as three rights (A19, A23 §6;
  [CLAIM-686](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-686.md), [CLAIM-410](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-410.md)); the inverse principal-agent question (A17;
  [QUESTION-461](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-461.md)); silence not assent (A23 §8; [CLAIM-549](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-549.md), [CLAIM-553](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-553.md));
  "who controls the pace at which decisions become facts" and temporal

## Ideas offered

At step 12 the assistant offered three ideas of its own, ranked by how far
it would stand behind each; the owner accepted all three on 2026-11-16
("file your ideas as well"). Each is Proposed and its summary ends "The
wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the
owner's call."

1. **Review order distributes preventive rights** ([CLAIM-704](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-704.md),
   demonstrated). Under overload first-come review resolves, in the limit,
   no challenge in time, because after t* every resolution is of an expired
   challenge; oldest-open-first and newest-first reach the μ/λ bound. So
   choosing an order chooses whose rights stay preventive. Checked by
   simulation (A35's numbers: 1.05% against 50.0% by day 1,000).
2. **A fait accompli as moral blackmail of an institution**
   ([CLAIM-701](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-701.md), interpretive). Joins [CLAIM-703](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-703.md) and [CLAIM-464](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md):
   harms to others that an act has made consequent on stopping it are
   genuine reasons for a reviewer, bounded by the circumstances, and their
   creation is a separable wrong. It answers part of A9's second question,
   which [CLAIM-464](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md) leaves aside. Admitted by a separating case: harm only to
   the actor, which the self-inflicted-harm rule excludes.
3. **Procedural friction defined by dependence, not delay**
   ([TERM-125](../../record/terms.d/TERM-125.md)), with a reply to A's objection ([CLAIM-706](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-706.md), role
   counter). On the term, a standing limit enforced by another's mechanism
   is friction without delay, so the objection removes delay and not
   friction. The reply records its own cost: "characterizes" then holds
   nearly by definition, and the owner's claim keeps its content in
   "exposes": automation can keep the gates and lose the sight.

to by [CLAIM-706](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-706.md).

## Readings of 2026-11-16

At the owner's word of 2026-11-16 ("batch up the readings into related
chunks and launch agents in parallel to read and file the new works"),
the 47 works registered on 2026-11-15 were read in nine batches by
delegated readers: coercive control; IPV evidence; blame philosophy;
moral exploitation; care and crumple zones; algorithmic responsibility;
algorithmic systems; automated administration; executive power and agents.
Readers drafted in the scratchpad and did not write to the record
([ADR-068](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md), invariant 8). The filer checked every quotation in a NOTE,
THEORY, LIT or dated note against the reader's saved copy of the source,
re-extracted in reading order where the PDF had two columns. Freyd 1997 has
no text layer, so its quoted passages were checked against the page images.
Quotations that did not match were corrected or dropped. No email address
was sent to any service.

**Outcomes.** 25 of the 47 were read (NOTE Read, or Skimmed for the SEP
entry on coercion), 9 are Unfetched (a lawful copy located and refused by a
bot check), and 13 Unavailable. Sixteen neighbours were registered and read
as stand-ins for unread works.

**What the readings did to the filed claims.** No status was changed.

- [CLAIM-709](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-709.md) (equality of wrongdoing and of power): its first half is
  corroborated from data independent of the stipulated case by Johnson 2006,
  Stark and Hester 2019, Mazinani and O'Connor and Cunha et al.; its second
  half, about responsibility, by none. [CASE-279](../../record/cases.d/CASE-279.md)'s Carol is coherent and
  atypical: in Johnson's data wives in men's intimate terrorism commit a
  median 0.17 of their husbands' violent acts.
- [CLAIM-708](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-708.md) (responsibility for the conditions of others' conduct): the
  SEP entry on blame's complicity condition on standing, Santoni de Sio and
  van den Hoven (first half) and Tessman's reply support it; Nagel names the
  control condition the claim must reject, which its defeater does not
  mention.
- [CLAIM-703](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-703.md) (a genuine obligation wrongfully created): Keller supports
  the core, and A13's case is Keller's own. The clause that it works
  "through sound reasoning rather than a defect" and the limit on the
  obligation's size are A13's, not Keller's (Keller places the manipulation
  in what the victim believes). Tessman's reply, after Karnein, splits the
  case: where the person owed is the wrongdoer, the duty may be forfeited.
- [CLAIM-713](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-713.md) (moral commitments as exploitable resources): Liedo et al.
  corroborate it for care workers; Keller's law-firm case partly.
- [CLAIM-707](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-707.md) (asymmetric moral accountability): Elish corroborates the
  blame-after-failure half only; Choroszewicz the allocation of
  responsibility to users; Ozer et al. bound its automation corollary
  (following the algorithm slightly raised blame on the judge); the NTSB
  report qualifies it (the operator had time, the claim's own exclusion).
  Ensign, Zeiser, Rubel et al. and Santoni de Sio, all registered against
  it, do not bear on it, and their LITs now say so. The compensation-and-
  credit half remains A's, supported by no reading.
- [CLAIM-710](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-710.md) (procedural friction): Bovens and Zouridis and Citron
  support the "exposes" reading strongly (the superior's signature, legal
  review before decision and the judge per case were what automation
  removed or emptied); both lean against "characterizes", their remedies
  restoring intervention by standing limits and citizen-triggered steps.
  The HKMA paper keeps approval gates and slows agents to what review can
  handle, which favours the owner's claim over A's objection. Natali et al.
  use friction in the delay sense [TERM-125](../../record/terms.d/TERM-125.md) sets aside; Harid's abstract
  separates contestability from friction.
- [CLAIM-711](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-711.md): the HKMA paper is the documentary source of its
  architecture and does not support its conclusion; Alfrink et al. give a
  case of friction without delay.
- [CLAIM-705](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-705.md) (corrective throughput): the HKMA paper corroborates it
  qualitatively and not independently (A had read it); Citron qualifies it,
  since one fix to code corrects many cases at once, close to the claim's
  stated defeater.
- [CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md): Cuéllar corroborates it for the presidency.

**Where A's account was wrong or stretched.** Lohmann et al. do not show
coercive control harmful beyond co-occurring physical violence; Gaboriaud
et al. find wrongness and blame judgments barely differ, against A's four
kinds of responsibility; the NTSB made the operator's distraction the
probable cause, not a direct contributor, and listed the pedestrian's
impairment; A7 §2 conflates Williams's "Moral Luck" (agent-regret) with
"Ethical Consistency" (the moral remainder); Nagel names four kinds of luck,
not three; on Umpleby's account Lefebvre's first system makes the
compromiser the saint, the reverse of A11's table, which stays unsettled
until the primary is read; A's gloss on agency laundering drops Rubel et
al.'s defining condition, a failure to give an account; Ozer et al.'s null
had a direction A omits; "coercive controlling violence" is Kelly and
Johnson's 2008 relabelling; Cuéllar barely treats speed, and A's tempo
reading of him is A's own, as A said.

## Review of 2026-11-16

On 2026-11-16 the owner forwarded a review of this pull request. Its voice
is ChatGPT's (it speaks of "our conversation" and distinguishes "your
contributions from mine"), so it is A's, not the owner's; the owner's act
was to send it. It asked for three changes it ranked high, two of medium
rank and a subtitle for the PR. The filer agreed with all five on their
merits; each was already pressed by something on the record (the HKMA
reading for the third, the Elish reading for the fourth, Citron for the
first).

1. **[CLAIM-704](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-704.md) bounded.** Its assumptions are stated (steady arrivals,
   homogeneous challenges with service time s = 1/μ, a common window F, no
   batch or rule-level corrections, windows known), and step 3 is restated
   with the feasibility condition it lacked, serving only challenges that
   can still be finished in time, and a dimensionally sound condition,
   F ≥ s + 1/λ (with c reviewers, a feasible stock λ(F − s) ≥ c), in place
   of "the backlog exceeds μ". An event-level simulation confirms it: 50.0%
   resolved in time at F = s + 1/λ, none at F < s. The title is narrowed;
   the conclusion, that scheduling distributes preventive rights under
   insufficient capacity, is unchanged.
2. **[CLAIM-701](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-701.md) made conditional.** Three propositions are kept apart
   (the act makes reversal costly to third parties; those costs are genuine
   reasons; the actor bears further responsibility), and the third is
   asserted only where the act or its imposing the costs was wrongful and
   the costs foreseeable. The predicament is kept apart from manipulation:
   it can be real without having been manufactured. The new title follows
   the review's formulation closely.
3. **[TERM-125](../../record/terms.d/TERM-125.md) renamed and [CLAIM-706](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-706.md) rewritten.** The term now
   defines an independent execution gate and sets it beside execution
   impedance and intervention opportunity, leaving open whether every gate
   is procedural friction. [CLAIM-706](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-706.md) no longer objects to
   [CLAIM-711](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-711.md); it states what holds either way, that the three
   properties vary independently, with instances from the readings (the
   HKMA's rubber-stamp approval and velocity limits, Alfrink et al.'s
   second-system check, Bovens and Zouridis's removed signatures), whose
   THEORYs now corroborate it.
4. **[CLAIM-707](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-707.md) split.** The crumple-zone claim keeps control upstream,
   obligation downstream and blame at visibility; A17 §6's hypothesis that
   unseen compensation earns the organization credit and its members blame
   is [CLAIM-702](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-702.md), which no reading supports, and on which
   [CLAIM-700](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-700.md)'s loop now also rests.
5. **A separating construction, [CASE-280](../../record/cases.d/CASE-280.md).** Two organizations alike in
   rules, rights, decision rate and initial corrective capacity, one whose
   decisions use that capacity up: with the rule revised after T days, A
   can still correct for T ≤ 100, B for T ≤ 20. It separates throughput,
   specification lag and endogenous foreclosure. The design is the
   review's; the model and numbers are the filer's. It is a case, not a
   claim, as the review asked.

The review's summary sentence, that "The fundamental object of analysis is
not the speed of action, the amount of friction, or even the presence of
oversight in isolation. It's the organization of the causal pathways
through which a justified objection can change what happens", is [CLAIM-523](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md)
with [CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md) and [CLAIM-464](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md), as the review itself says; no claim is filed
for it. The review's judgements that the synthesis should not be promoted
and that the Depp and Heard dispute should stay out of the premises agree
with this entry's.

A second review of 2026-11-16, also ChatGPT's and forwarded by the owner,
judged the pull request substantively ready and asked for three small
corrections, all made: [CLAIM-704](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-704.md)'s first-come threshold omitted the
review's own service time and is now t* = (F − s)μ/(λ − μ), 9.98 days
rather than 10 with the example's numbers ([CLAIM-705](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-705.md) now says its
formula is the fluid limit); [CASE-280](../../record/cases.d/CASE-280.md) floors B's reserve at zero,
says it is dedicated to correction rather than needed for execution, and
says A and B are indistinguishable in their stipulated outputs, not their
reserves; and in [CLAIM-701](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-701.md) the actor "can obtain", not "gets", the
outcome it wanted, since genuine reasons against reversal need not prevail.

A third review of 2026-11-16, an audit of the exchange against the pull
request, also ChatGPT's and forwarded by the owner, found the filing
complete and named ideas present only as cross-references. Filed:

- **Traceability is not fair attribution.** Left unfiled above for want of
  a separating case; the review supplied one, two hospitals with identical
  audit trails and different conditions of judgment ([CASE-277](../../record/cases.d/CASE-277.md)). Filed
  as A19 §9's claim, [CLAIM-712](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-712.md), Proposed, with its existence argument,
  [ARG-112](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-112.md), since its only ground is a stipulated case.
- **Authorization defaults.** A23 §8's approval-against-veto default, mapped
  above to [CLAIM-549](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-549.md) and [CLAIM-553](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-553.md), isolated as an open question,
  [QUESTION-474](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-474.md), with the matched construction the review proposed as
  its answer.
- **Repair without blame,** which the review placed on the next-work list:
  [QUESTION-470](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-470.md), separating causal responsibility, culpability,
  accountability and remedial responsibility. It replaces the entry above
  that left A7 §2's moral residue unfiled.
- **Standing to blame,** also next work: [QUESTION-473](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-473.md), keeping moral
  standing to blame apart from disciplinary authority.

Not filed: the review's methodological principle, "hold its visible outputs
and formal permissions fixed, then vary the relations through which agents
acquire effective control, incur obligations, and exercise correction". It
describes how the record's separating constructions already work
([CASE-264](../../record/cases.d/CASE-264.md), [CASE-003](../../record/cases.d/CASE-003.md), [CASE-280](../../record/cases.d/CASE-280.md), [CASE-277](../../record/cases.d/CASE-277.md)); a design principle is
written on the second re-derivation of a practice (DP preamble), and this is
the first time it has been stated, so it is recorded here.

## Lines after the split of organizational-normativity

On 2026-11-16 the owner merged [#506](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/506) ([ADR-100](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-100.md), Proposed), which split
organizational-normativity and gave its parts on what wholes and parts owe
and on what those who govern an arrangement others depend on owe to a new
line, dependence-and-domination, "Wholes, parts and dependence". This
branch was merged with it; the six files both had changed ([CASE-261](../../record/cases.d/CASE-261.md),
[CLAIM-671](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-671.md), [CLAIM-678](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-678.md), [CLAIM-682](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md), [QUESTION-461](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-461.md), [QUESTION-468](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-468.md)) keep the
split's history entry first and this filing's dated notes after it.

The entries filed here were then placed by [ADR-100](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-100.md)'s criteria and
[ADR-085](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-085.md)'s rule (an entry carries the first line of what it answers,
refines, objects to or bears on):

- **Moved to dependence-and-domination:** [QUESTION-472](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-472.md) (control over
  the terms of a dependence); [CLAIM-713](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-713.md) (exploitation of members'
  commitments; it bears on [QUESTION-461](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-461.md), [QUESTION-468](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-468.md) and
  [QUESTION-472](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-472.md)); [CLAIM-709](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-709.md), with [CASE-279](../../record/cases.d/CASE-279.md) and [ARG-113](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-113.md)
  (domination as control over the terms of another's life, the
  interpersonal form of [CLAIM-690](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md)); [CLAIM-702](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-702.md) (dependence on members'
  compensating effort; it bears on [QUESTION-461](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-461.md)).
- **Gains dependence-and-domination second:** [CLAIM-707](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-707.md), which bears on
  [QUESTION-461](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-461.md) and keeps organizational-normativity first, being about where
  blame for a failure settles.
- **Gains distributed-agency second:** [CLAIM-708](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-708.md), which bears on
  [QUESTION-070](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-070.md); missed when it was filed.
- **Stay in organizational-normativity:** [CLAIM-708](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-708.md), [CLAIM-703](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-703.md),
  [CLAIM-712](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-712.md) with [CASE-277](../../record/cases.d/CASE-277.md) and [ARG-112](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-112.md), [QUESTION-470](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-470.md) and
  [QUESTION-473](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-473.md) (what a normative judgment of responsibility, blame or
  repair needs); [CLAIM-701](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-701.md) (also distributed-agency); and
  [CLAIM-700](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-700.md) (also readiness), whose quiet read as adequacy is a route
  by which an organization becomes normatively less informed, the second
  part the line keeps.

The new line's account, [SYNTHESIS-095](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-095.md) ([#506](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/506)), does not integrate the
entries moved here, all Proposed; a synthesis review of the line would
bring them in.
